findings.description: Critical: an orphaned setup reservation permanently blocks every sync point with no expiry, GC, or operator escape. `setupReservation` carries only `created_at`/`updated_at` — no TTL, no `expires_at` — while `specs/worktree/spec.md` ("Provisioning reservation blocks sync points") and the CLI `safety_invariants` make an unpublished reservation an indeterminate blocker. Reconciliation is reserved exclusively to the original actor: setup-and-acquire states "Retry reconciles only the exact same setup_id, generation, and requested triple" and "a different setup or controller MUST NOT consume, overwrite, or clean up those side effects". No command in `commands:` operates on reservations (there is no reservation list/abandon/reconcile), `recovery adopt`/`force-adopt` key on entries, and the GC invariant mentions only retained entries. Unlike leases, whose bounded 30-minute TTL is the whole point of D4, a reservation left behind by a controller that never returns is unbounded — reintroducing precisely the permanent sync-point deadlock this change exists to remove, and doing so on the crash path rather than the happy path.
findings.resolution: Give reservations a bounded lifetime with the same shape as leases: add a required `expires_at`/`ttl_seconds` to `setupReservation`, and specify that an expired reservation stops being a sync-point blocker and becomes eligible for locked, generation-fenced quarantine (never silent side-effect deletion). Add an explicit operator command (e.g. `worktree.py reservation abandon SETUP_ID --entry-generation G --reason R`) that converts an expired reservation into a `setup-failure` quarantine entry, add the corresponding worktree spec scenario, and cover expired-reservation unblocking in task 1.3/1.5.

findings.description: Critical: the feature-HEAD completion barrier is unowned — it has no declaration in the artifact the scheduler actually reads. `contracts/prerequisites.yaml` puts `execution_gate.completion_visibility: feature-head` and `dependent_base_rule: exact-verified-feature-head` in a contract file, but `wp-baseline-preflight` in `work-packages.yaml` declares only `worktree: {name: phase-lifecycle-baseline-preflight, mode: shared}` — no barrier field, no completion-visibility field. Task 0.5 is written as "packages **declaring** a feature-HEAD barrier are not marked complete until…", yet nothing declares one. `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/dag_scheduler.py:142` copies `package.get("worktree", {})` through verbatim and `mark_completed()` (line 343) has no notion of a commit, HEAD, or branch lock; `mode: shared` appears nowhere else in any `work-packages.yaml` in the repository and is interpreted by no code. As written, the barrier requirement in `specs/skill-workflow/spec.md` ("Prerequisite Evidence SHALL Be Visible Before Dependent Dispatch") is untestable because the scheduler cannot tell which packages it applies to.
findings.resolution: Add an explicit package-level declaration to the work-packages schema and to `wp-baseline-preflight` (e.g. `completion: {visibility: feature-head, evidence_path: …, dependent_base_rule: exact-verified-feature-head}`), and reference `contracts/prerequisites.yaml` from it rather than storing the gate only there. Extend task 0.5's file list to include the work-packages schema/validator so the new key is validated, and make task 0.4's regression test assert the scheduler reads the declaration (not a hard-coded package id).

findings.description: Critical: two requirements in the same delta spec give contradictory worktree rules for the preflight package. "Implementation Orchestrator Worktree Setup" (MODIFIED) states "The implementation orchestrator SHALL create a dedicated worktree and fenced lease for **every root or parallel work package** before mutation", while "Prerequisite Evidence SHALL Be Visible Before Dependent Dispatch" (ADDED) states "The authoritative prerequisite preflight SHALL execute as a **root package in the managed shared feature worktree**". A conforming implementation cannot satisfy both for `wp-baseline-preflight`. `work-packages.yaml` compounds the ambiguity by giving the package both `mode: shared` and a package-specific `worktree.name: phase-lifecycle-baseline-preflight`, which is the naming of an isolated per-package checkout, not the shared feature checkout. An implementer following the MODIFIED requirement will produce an isolated preflight whose verified commit is not feature HEAD — silently defeating D15's stated rationale ("its verified commit is feature HEAD rather than an isolated result awaiting final integration").
findings.resolution: Carve the exception into the MODIFIED requirement explicitly ("every root or parallel work package **except a package declaring feature-HEAD completion visibility, which runs in the managed shared feature worktree under the parent phase lease**"), and drop or repurpose `worktree.name` for the shared-mode package so the two artifacts agree on which checkout is used.

findings.description: Critical: no command can dispose an entry that has no activity lease, and the existing `teardown --force` path is silently dropped. The contract makes `--owner`, `--lease-id`, `--controller-instance-id`, and `--entry-generation` all required for `teardown`, but three documented states have `activity_lease: null`: normalized v1 entries, compatibility `setup` entries (which the contract explicitly says store a null target and stay unleased), and every entry that `release-session`/`release-owner`/unsafe finalization has quarantined-and-cleared. For those, no lease id exists to supply. The recovery route is also closed for legacy state: `recovery adopt` requires stale same-host process evidence, and a v1 entry has no evidence file at all ("missing … evidence is indeterminate" → exit 7), forcing `recovery force-adopt`, which for a null durability target "require[s] durability-remote and durability-ref together, validate[s] and fetch[es] that exact bound target" — impossible for a legacy branch that was never pushed. Separately, today's `skills/worktree/scripts/worktree.py` teardown carries `--force`, documented in its own help text as "Used by POST /agents/{id}/kick to clear stale entries"; the contract omits it and the worktree spec says teardown "SHALL NOT use force to bypass the condition", while `safety_invariants` still assumes "an existing explicit operator force path" exists. Migration compatibility is asserted only for setup, branch override, isolation detection, and package layout — teardown is not covered.
findings.resolution: Add a lease-optional disposal form (identity args required only when a live lease exists, `--entry-generation` always required) so unleased and quarantine-cleared entries can be removed after the same dirty/durability checks. Explicitly state whether `teardown --force` survives; if it does, add it to the contract with its safety envelope and a scenario for the coordinator kick path; if it does not, name the replacement the kick endpoint must call and add it to `wp-coordinator-projections`' scope. Add a recovery path for a null-target legacy entry whose branch was never pushed (force-adopt with an explicit no-remote acknowledgement) rather than requiring a ref that cannot exist.

findings.description: Critical: the inventory fails its own completeness rule, and one real consumer sits outside every package's write scope. The MODIFIED invariant says the inventory "SHALL cover every canonical consumer of setup, heartbeat, pin, active-agent, and registry state and automated tests MUST fail for an unclassified consumer". Scanning canonical sources finds unclassified consumers: `agent-coordinator/src/coordination_api.py` (its `/worktrees/active` docstring encodes the exact semantics being removed — "Omits stale entries (heartbeat > 1h); pinned entries always included"), `agent-coordinator/src/event_stream.py:197` (publishes the worktree projection to SSE clients under the key `active_agents`, a UI-facing activity label), `agent-coordinator/src/sync_points.py` (touched by tasks 5.1/5.2 but absent from the inventory, which lists only `worktrees_view.py` under `coordinator-projections`), `skills/context-engineering/SKILL.md`, and `skills/worktree/SKILL.md`. In the other direction, `project-context-refresh-sync-point` is classified as a consumer although `skills/project-context-refresh/SKILL.md` has no registry or active-agent usage. Worse, neither `coordination_api.py` nor `event_stream.py` appears in any package's `write_allow` (`wp-coordinator-projections` allows only sync_points/worktrees_view/openspec_proposals_api/kanban_viz/Dockerfile/tests), so the required removal of stale pinned-as-activity prose and labels cannot be performed in scope. Additionally, `session-hooks` is classified `registry_reader`, but D10 and the "Session Finalization" requirement have it invoke `release-session`, which quarantines entries and clears leases — a mutation no reader mode permits.
findings.resolution: Add the missing consumers with correct modes (`coordination_api`, `event_stream`, `sync_points` as registry_reader/projection; `context-engineering` and `worktree` SKILL.md as documentation consumers or an explicit exemption list), remove or justify `project-context-refresh-sync-point`, and introduce a distinct mode for hooks (e.g. `session_backstop`) rather than `registry_reader`. Extend `wp-coordinator-projections.scope.write_allow` with `agent-coordinator/src/coordination_api.py` and `agent-coordinator/src/event_stream.py`, and make task 2.7's completeness scan assert against the actual grep set so it fails today.

findings.description: Critical: the `quarantined` envelope transition is the one autopilot recovery write that a stale controller can still make. D9 fences only two classes: "Every `present` or `teardown_pending` envelope mutation also proves the exact live registry owner/lease/controller triple plus entry generation before CAS", and after registry deletion "only the expected `teardown_pending -> removed` CAS is allowed, bound to unchanged envelope generation, lease id, entry generation, and finalization intent". `checkout_state: quarantined` is written after quarantine-plus-clear, when no live registry lease remains to prove — so the registry-triple precondition is by construction unavailable, and D9 states no substitute binding for it. A displaced controller holding `lease-old` that reloads the latest envelope generation therefore satisfies the only stated guard (monotonic CAS) and can drive an actively resumed run — one that legitimately rotated to `lease-new` via `lease resume` — into `quarantined`, where D9's own rule ("Partial presence, `teardown_pending`, quarantine, missing/non-durable refs, or identity mismatch remains escalated") makes it unrecoverable without operator action. This is exactly the stale-controller write the design elsewhere takes care to prevent.
findings.resolution: Bind the `quarantined` CAS to the quarantining actor's identity: require the write to carry the prior lease id plus entry generation and to match the `recovery_context` (prior_owner/prior_lease_id/prior_controller_instance_id) the registry recorded in the same quarantine transaction, refusing when the registry's recovery context names a different lease. State the rule in D9 alongside the pending-to-removed rule and add it to task 4.3's fault matrix.

findings.description: Nit: resume is not specified to refuse a completed run. The schema's second `allOf` branch permits `checkout_state: removed` together with `finalization_intent: done`, and D9's recreation rule keys only on removed state plus exact-tip equality: "resume verifies the currently configured remote URL digest, fetches the stored ref, and requires its tip to equal `durable_head` exactly … recreates the worktree and registry entry … and only then dispatches", continuing "from the phase derived from canonical state". The corresponding spec scenario scopes itself to "ESCALATE or exception finalization recorded `checkout_state=removed`" but nothing forbids the `done` case. Re-invoking a run that already reached DONE and opened its PR would recreate the disposed checkout, take a new lease, and re-dispatch phases against a branch the human merge gate already owns.
findings.resolution: State in D9 and the recovery-envelope contract that `finalization_intent: done` with `checkout_state: removed` is terminal: resume reports the completed run and refuses recreation, requiring an explicit new run id. Add the case to task 4.3's test list next to the advanced/rewound/missing-ref refusals.

findings.description: Nit: task 2.8's declared file scope exceeds its package's write_allow, so the task as written cannot be executed inside `wp-lifecycle-consumers`. Task 2.8 targets "inventory-owned launcher skills under `skills/`, excluding `skills/autopilot/**` and `skills/merge-pull-requests/**`", which literally includes the `standalone_owner` entries `plan-feature`, `implement-feature`, `iterate-on-plan`, `iterate-on-implementation`, and `validate-feature`. None of those paths appear in `wp-lifecycle-consumers.scope.write_allow`; they belong to `wp-phase-lifecycle`, which migrates them in task 2.2. The scope checker will either reject the writes or the agent will interpret the exclusion list as exhaustive and re-migrate skills another package already owns.
findings.resolution: Restate task 2.8's file scope as the explicit `wp-lifecycle-consumers` set (archive-roadmap, autopilot-roadmap, changelog-version, explore-feature, fix-scrub, plan-roadmap, prototype-feature, quick-task, refresh-architecture) and note that the five phase launchers are migrated by task 2.2 in `wp-phase-lifecycle`.

findings.description: Nit: whether the continuous autopilot lease carries a `session_id` is never decided, and the two artifacts that touch it assume opposite answers. `lease acquire`/`setup-and-acquire` make `--session-id` optional; D9 lists what autopilot passes into every phase (owner, lease id, controller id) and never mentions a session id. The skill-workflow scenario "Session end releases only matching owners" assumes autopilot's session id is "different or null" and must be left untouched, while D10 explicitly contemplates the opposite — "If it quarantines a continuous checkout, later resume preserves the envelope/registry mismatch and remains ESCALATE until explicit reconciliation." Since autopilot runs inside an orchestrating session, the choice decides whether an ordinary interrupted run resumes cleanly or requires `recovery force-adopt` with actor, rationale, and termination confirmation every time.
findings.resolution: Decide and record it in D9: either autopilot deliberately acquires with a null session id (the crash backstop is then TTL expiry plus explicit reconciliation) or it supplies the session id and accepts quarantine-on-session-end as intended behaviour. Whichever is chosen, state it in the "Autopilot SHALL Hold One Continuous Owner Lease" requirement so the session-hook scenario and D10 stop implying different contracts.

findings.description: Nit: two task traceability references do not resolve against the delta specs. Task 2.3 cites `skill-workflow` — "Package integration proves parent-ref durability"; no scenario of that name exists in any spec file (the nearest is "Worktrees are finalized after integration" under "Implementation Orchestrator Worktree Setup"). Task 1.1 cites "Activity lease commands respect environment isolation", which is a Requirement heading, not a scenario; the scenario is "Lease mutations short-circuit under harness isolation". Traceability checks and reviewers matching tasks to acceptance scenarios will silently drop coverage for the package-durability behaviour, which is the exact contract task 2.4 implements.
findings.resolution: Repoint task 2.3 to "Worktrees are finalized after integration" (or add a real scenario with the cited name asserting the push-parent-then-prove-package-HEAD ordering), and repoint task 1.1 to "Lease mutations short-circuit under harness isolation".

findings.description: Nit: the classification schema enforces one row of the truth table and leaves the two equally mandatory rows to producers. The top-level `allOf` encodes `marker_status ∈ {conflicting, duplicate, invalid} → delivery_stage: ambiguous`, but the merge-pull-requests truth table's first row ("incomplete, truncated, or failed" required evidence → `ambiguous`) has no corresponding constraint on `evidence.diff_status`, and `evidence.base_state.inspection_status`/`head_state.inspection_status == failed` — which D11 says "are represented explicitly and always yield `ambiguous`" — is likewise unconstrained. The asymmetry is a trap: a producer bug that stamps `implementation` on a truncated diff passes schema validation, and the contracts README's "Producers additionally enforce the exhaustive truth table" is the only thing standing between that bug and an unsafe archival route.
findings.resolution: Add two more `allOf` branches mirroring the marker rule: `if evidence.diff_status ∈ {truncated, failed} then delivery_stage const ambiguous`, and the same for either `proposalState.inspection_status == failed`. This makes the fail-safe rows machine-checked rather than prose, at no cost to the producers that already comply.

findings.description: Optional: the preflight package edits the scheduler it depends on, from the checkout that scheduler is running in. `wp-baseline-preflight` declares `mode: shared` (design D15: "runs in the managed shared feature worktree") and its write set includes `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/dag_scheduler.py` and `integration_orchestrator.py`. Task ordering compounds this: 0.3 runs the live resolver and commits `baseline-gates.json` to gate dependents, but the barrier that is supposed to enforce that gating is only implemented in 0.5, two tasks later. For this change's own coordinated run, the scheduler in effect while `wp-pr-delivery` and `wp-phase-lifecycle` are unblocked is either the pre-change scheduler (no barrier) or a mid-edit one. The `depends_on` edges still serialize dispatch, so the risk is bounded, but the stronger guarantee the plan advertises — dependents created from the exact verified feature HEAD — is not actually in force during the change that introduces it.
findings.resolution: Note the bootstrap explicitly in task 0.3: during this change's own execution the barrier is enforced manually (verify `baseline-gates.json` is on feature HEAD before dispatching dependents) and the new scheduler code takes effect only for subsequent changes. Consider moving the scheduler edits (0.4/0.5) into a separate package that does not run in shared mode, so no package rewrites the orchestrator executing it.

findings.description: FYI: nothing states the retention policy for `.git-worktrees/.autopilot-runs/<run-id>/recovery.json`. The envelope lives beside the registry inside `.git-worktrees/`, which `worktree.py gc` walks, yet the GC safety invariants speak only of registry entries and retained worktrees, and D9 never says when an envelope in `checkout_state: removed` with `finalization_intent: done` is deleted. Over time the directory accumulates one entry per run, and a GC implementation that treats unknown `.git-worktrees/` children as sweepable could delete a `teardown_pending` envelope that is the only record able to reconcile a crashed teardown.
findings.resolution: State in D9 or the contracts README that GC must not touch `.git-worktrees/.autopilot-runs/`, and give a bounded cleanup rule (e.g. envelopes in `removed` state are eligible for deletion after a documented retention window; `present`, `teardown_pending`, and `quarantined` envelopes are never swept).

findings.description: The package-teardown durability proof is achievable against the repository's actual integration strategy. D8 requires that successful package integration "first pushes the parent feature ref, then proves the exact package HEAD is reachable from its stored parent-feature durability target", and `skills/worktree/scripts/merge_worktrees.py:217` integrates with `git merge --no-ff`, which preserves the package tip as an ancestor of the feature branch. The rule therefore holds without changing integration topology, and the contract's decision to store the parent feature remote ref as the package entry's durability target ("Package and automatic workflow callers MUST use setup-and-acquire and store the parent feature remote ref as the durability target, not a disposable child branch") correctly avoids requiring child branches to be pushed under their own names.
findings.resolution: No change required; consider asserting the `--no-ff` dependency in the task 2.3 test so a future switch to squash or rebase integration fails loudly instead of quarantining every package worktree.

findings.description: Timestamp-free setup intent traces cleanly and consistently from schema through CLI, design, and spec. `leaseIntent` deliberately omits `acquired_at`, `last_heartbeat`, and `expires_at` while requiring the full ownership triple, and its `lifecycle_mode` enum is correctly narrowed to `standalone|continuous` (excluding `manual`, which only recovery leases use). `setupReservation` carries its own `created_at`/`updated_at` so reservation age is observable without ever implying lease liveness. The CLI's setup-and-acquire step says publication derives `acquired_at` and `last_heartbeat` from one timestamp and `expires_at` from that timestamp plus the intent TTL, D2 says the same, and the worktree scenario "Fresh automatic setup publishes through a durable reservation" asserts it as an acceptance criterion. Four artifacts agree with no drift, which closes the class of bug where a lease appears to have been alive during a long checkout creation.

Operator-override binding and append-only invalidation are complete and internally consistent across schema, design, and spec. The `deliveryRouting` `allOf` forces `decision_source: classifier`, a null override, and blocked review/validation/cleanup routes whenever `effective_stage` is `ambiguous`; the state-level branch permits an override only while `latest_delivery_classification.delivery_stage` is `ambiguous` and otherwise pins `decision_source: classifier` with a null override, matching D15's "clear proposal, implementation, or mixed classifications require classifier routing and reject an override". `selected_stage == effective_stage` is enforced per stage rather than assumed. `operatorOverride` binds all five values D15 names (base_sha, head_sha, ruleset_version, `pr-delivery-v1+jcs-sha256`, digest), and `operatorOverrideEvent` requires the observed counterpart of each plus a `reason_code` enum that covers every mismatch class the spec enumerates — so the invalidation audit cannot be written without the evidence that justified it, and the history survives the override being cleared.
